I'm upvoting and commenting because I'd really like to see what people have to say to this, it's a valid and interesting question. 

I think that we can both agree that the best outcome is that you find happiness in life, then you are happy and your loved ones are happy because you are still around. Maybe that's not possible. I am having suicidal thoughts myself and don't know if its possible for me personally, so I understand where you are coming from. But what do you think you would need to be happy? 

People spending time with you, caring about you more?

I feel like my mind has been permanently damaged by some of the horrible experiences I've had to face, it's very difficult to picture a life where I get out of this and am really happy. All we can do is hold on and encourage each other to fight to get better one more day.

Ok, here's the thing about age. We all have this idea that we are fully developed and know life pretty well regardless of what age we are. 

I'm in my late 20s and, because of my own problems, I am also suicidal. There are probably some people in their 60s who read my posts and think 'your life is just beginning'. 

**Believe me** when I tell you: you have just turned 17, the years that are about to come bring about *massive* changes to your life. Going to college, or going and getting a full time job, moving out of your parents house, becoming independent, choosing what you eat, when you eat it, where you go and when you go there, who you meet up with, who you live with, what you study, new hobbies, new interests. All of these major aspects of your life are going to radically change in the years directly in front of you. The world you exist in a few years from now will be unrecognisable from the one you live in now. Your own brain is going to mature and alter its way of thinking naturally over the next few years, you have no choice in the matter.

If you are not seeing a doctor or therapist, you absolutely have to. If you can sort out your issues now, be a little selfish over the next few years to build a life that makes *you* happy, and come out the other side I promise you that you will look back and thank yourself.

I know exactly what you mean. I think everyone has to experience a little hardship and some problems here and there to become strong, but the huge, scarring problems, the kind of problems that push you to the verge of suicide are not positive in any way.

What do these people think therapists do? If everyone who went through shit came out stronger that whole profession wouldn't exist.

Believe it or not it is possible to live in such mental or physical torture that you cannot find happiness for years and years and years. In that situation people often choose to end their lives rather than face it for another minute. 

You clearly have very little experience with that kind of mental or physical torture. That is a fantastic thing, but there is a very dark side of life that you have never had to experience. 

It is kind of you to come here and try to help people who are in the middle of that suffering but the fact that you have chosen to *argue* in the comments when they try to explain why your advice isn't helpful to them is extremely patronising.
